question_text: BUDGET is to FINANCE as CURRICULUM is to ___?

hint_ladder.title: Plan-Field Pattern
hint_ladder.text: Budget is a plan in the field of Finance. So the analogy is 'plan : field'. What is the field for Curriculum?

hint_ladder.title: Curriculum's Domain
hint_ladder.text: A curriculum is an educational plan, so its field is Education. Not just any place or person involved.

hint_ladder.title: Eliminate Distractors
hint_ladder.text: School (A) is a location; Teacher (C) and Student (D) are roles. None represent the field itself. So the field is Education.

hint_ladder.title: Correct Answer
hint_ladder.text: Thus, the answer is Education, matching the 'plan : field' relationship exactly.

A.text: You might have chosen A because curriculum is used in school, but the analogy needs a field, not a place.

B.text: Correct. Budget is a finance plan, and curriculum is an education plan, so the relationship is plan : field.

C.text: You might have chosen C because teachers implement curriculum, but the analogy is about the domain, not the person.

D.text: You might have chosen D because students learn from curriculum, but the field is education, not the learners.

next_time_rule: In 'plan:field' analogies, focus on the broad domain not the specific place or role.
deconstruct_text:
A barangay captain creates a budget (plan) for finance to allocate funds for projects.

A school principal designs a curriculum (plan) for education to guide lessons for students.

So, the relationship is plan : field. The field for curriculum is Education, not the school building (place) or the people (teacher/student).
